article.headline: Afghanistan Stuns Australia by Four Wickets to Clinch Maiden Hong Kong Title
article.summary: Afghanistan secured their first-ever Hong Kong International Sixes championship on Sunday after successfully chasing down a 116-run target against Australia.
article.body: Imran Mir hammered an unbeaten 53 runs off just 14 deliveries to anchor the pursuit, while Farmanullah Safi remained not out on 27 from only seven balls. The pair combined with captain Gulbadin Naib’s 17-run contribution to overtake Australia’s first-innings score of 115 with four wickets and limited balls to spare. This clinical batting display ensured Afghanistan successfully navigated a challenging chase at the Mission Road Ground in Mong Kok to claim the tournament trophy. The victory marks a significant milestone for the team, as it represents their first title win in the history of the Hong Kong International Sixes. The Afghanistan Cricket Board lauded the result as an outstanding all-round performance from the national side. For cricket followers, this result demonstrates the growing competitive capacity of the Afghan squad in short-format matches, highlighting their ability to overhaul significant totals under pressure in tournament finals. Australia had initially set a formidable pace by posting 115 runs in their allotted six overs. However, the Afghan side’s aggressive batting approach effectively countered the Australian bowling lineup to seal the win on Sunday. The tournament concluded with the presentation of the maiden title to the Afghanistan team, cementing their successful campaign in the Hong Kong competition. This triumph adds a fresh chapter to the nation's cricketing record, confirming their momentum in international limited-overs contests.

news.og_title: India becomes first team to reach 400 T20I sixes in a calendar year
news.og_desc: India achieved this landmark during the fifth and final T20I against New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday. During the match, the back-to-back world champions hammered a total of 11 sixes, touching the 400-run mark.

news.title: India Becomes First Team To Smash 400 Sixes In Single Calendar Year After Naman Dhir’s Six Off Blair Tickner In 5th T20I
news.og_title: India Becomes First Team To Smash 400 Sixes In Single Calendar Year After Naman Dhir’s Six Off Blair Tickner In 5th T20I
news.og_desc: India becomes the first team to smash 400 sixes in a single calendar year after Naman Dhir’s six off Blair Tickner’s delivery in the 19th over of the ongoing fifth T20I in Hamilton. India have smashed 142 sixes against the Kiwis which is also the most against an opposition in T20Is.
